persona: Cognitive psychology student running a reaction time experiment with 30 participants, exported from E-Prime stimulus presentation software
source_style: exported directly from E-Prime behavioral experiment log to CSV

columns.name: Reaction Time (ms)
columns.notes: Latency in milliseconds from stimulus onset to button press, range ~220–750ms

clean_table: First 5 rows + last 2 rows. Total 1440 data rows (30 participants × 48 trials). Generation rule: RT = base_condition_stimulus + participant_offset + N(0, 60); accuracy 85–98% conditional on stimulus type and modality. Visual targets fastest (~420ms, 94% accuracy), auditory distractors slowest (~510ms, 83% accuracy). All rows complete, no missing values.
intended_analysis: Does reaction time differ by condition (visual vs. auditory)? Is there a stimulus type effect (target vs. distractor)? What is the interaction: are visual targets faster than auditory targets? What proportion of responses are accurate in each condition? Is there a speed-accuracy tradeoff?
what_a_naive_reader_would_get_wrong: Nothing obvious—this is a standard, tidy CSV export from a behavioral experiment. Column types are consistent throughout. A naive reader should parse it correctly.
